item.title: Comunidad en Merrimack aliviada de que el DHS abandone su plan de centro de detención
item.description: La gobernadora Kelly Ayotte anunció el martes que el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional de EE.UU. no seguirá con la propuesta de construir una instalación del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas en Merrimack.

item.title: Legislation about gender identity is back on the table in the NH State House
item.description: The House Judiciary Committee considered bills on restricting bathroom use based on sex assigned at birth, and a bill to eliminate gender identity protections from state law.

item.title: Merrimack no tendrá un centro de ICE. Legisladores discuten vertederos, vacunación en escuelas.
item.description: La gobernadora Kelly Ayotte anunció el martes que el DHS está abandonando sus planes para un centro de detención de ICE en Merrimack.

item.title: Plan your Weekend in NH: Stingrays, snowshoes, and ABBA
item.description: Feed stingrays, dance to disco, track wildlife, catch Olympic-level ice dance, or celebrate Pokemon Day during this midwinter weekend across the Granite State.

item.title: As state seeks literacy answers, small rural schools offer clues to student success
item.description: As Gov. Kelly Ayotte tasks the New Hampshire Department of Education with examining the factors driving successful literacy education at the highest-performing schools, the Concord Monitor’s analysis could offer some hints as to what the department will find.

item.title: Jenny Lawson is the latest guest of 'Authors on Main' on April 1
item.description: Join NHPR at the Capitol Center for the Arts on Wed., April 1, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. for Authors on Main featuring best selling author Jenny Lawson. Lawson will be in conversation with NHPR’s Rebecca Lavoie about her latest work, "How to Be Okay When Nothing is Okay".

item.title: Summer camp, churches, and coffin workshop added to NH Register of Historic Places
item.description: The New Hampshire State Register of Historic Places encourages the protection of significant buildings, districts, sites, landscapes, structures and objects that are considered meaningful to the history and traditions of the state.

item.title: State to ask Supreme Court to overturn Claremont school funding rulings
item.description: The Attorney General’s Office plans to ask the state Supreme Court to overturn its two landmark Claremont school funding rulings from the 1990s, arguing they are an improper reading of New Hampshire's constitution.
